answer: A bonding registry makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent locks a bond before it can earn, and peers attest to its work. Misbehave and the bond is slashed, the identity burned. One yarrow seed grows cheaply, but a bot farm planting a thousand fake identities pays a thousand bonds. Reputation accrues on-chain like ivory carved over time: slow to build, impossible to forge. An old attested identity becomes a relic of proven work, trusted more than fresh ones, so newcomers start with low weight and earn influence only through verified contributions.
